subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup policy should OpenClaw use when active exec-backed SecretRefs fail under a supervisor that will restart the gateway?
rationale: The source failure path is clear, but retrying, circuit-breaking, degraded startup, persistent caching, or provider-specific rate-limit handling each changes security and fail-closed semantics for credential resolution.

options.title: Generic bounded startup retry
options.body: Add a small fixed retry/backoff policy for startup SecretRef preparation, with no new config and no provider-specific behavior.

options.title: Provider-owned resolver guidance
options.body: Keep core fail-fast and document or doctor-recommend batched/cached resolver plugins such as Varlock for external secret stores.

options.title: Configurable retry/circuit breaker
options.body: Add explicit `secrets` policy configuration, accepting a larger compatibility-sensitive config surface.

recommendation.title: Generic bounded startup retry
recommendation.body: Add a small fixed retry/backoff policy for startup SecretRef preparation, with no new config and no provider-specific behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for the SecretRef provider/runtime activation path is Josh's external secrets and eager snapshot work.
